title: Obex inherits Sky's base-class Risk Capital requirements, with changes propagating automatically into the Obex Artifact
content:
A.6.1.1.5.2.6.1.2.1.3.2 states that as operators of the Obex Liquidity Layer, "Treadstone automatically inherits, and is subject to, the base class of operational requirements related to Total Risk Capital management defined in A.2.2.10.1.1.3.2.1.2 - Primes' Total Risk Capital (TRC) Management. **Modifications to the base operational logic automatically propagate to the Obex Artifact.**"

The vocabulary is deliberately object-oriented, and the semantics match: the Agent's Artifact holds a live reference to a shared base class rather than a copy of it. Sky can tighten TRC requirements once and have the change bind every Prime Agent immediately, with no per-Agent amendment, no coordination problem, and no possibility of Agents drifting onto stale versions of the rules.

The tension with the rest of Obex's governance is direct and worth stating. A.6.1.1.5.2.2.2.2.1.2.1 builds an elaborate amendment path for the Artifact — a 1% proposal threshold, a Facilitator alignment review, a three-day token holder vote. This clause routes around all of it: a category of binding obligation enters the Artifact without any Obex actor consenting, voting, or even being notified by the mechanism itself.

That is defensible where the obligations are prudential rather than discretionary — an Agent should not be able to vote itself out of the ecosystem's risk rules, and requiring per-Agent ratification would make system-wide risk changes hostage to the slowest Agent. But it does mean the Obex Artifact is not self-contained. Reading it in full at any moment does not tell you what Obex is bound to, because part of the text is a pointer whose target can change underneath it.
